The Beat Generation rose in the 1950s and 1960s amid post-World War II disillusionment, growing interest in alternative music such as jazz, and rejection of conventional values. Beat writers drew inspiration from jazz musicians including Charlie Parker and John Coltrane.

Beat Generation writers challenged traditional literary structures through stream-of-consciousness writing, spontaneous prose, free verse, surreal imagery, and personal or autobiographical subject matter. Their writing often criticized mainstream culture and focused on individual experience.

Examples of prominent Beat Generation writers and works include Jack Kerouac (On the Road, The Dharma Bums, Big Sur, The Subterraneans); Allen Ginsberg (Howl and Other Poems, Kaddish and Other Poems, The Fall of America: Poems of These States); William S. Burroughs (Naked Lunch, Junky, The Soft Machine, The Ticket That Exploded); Lawrence Ferlinghetti (A Coney Island of the Mind, Pictures of the Gone World, Starting from San Francisco); and Diane di Prima (Memoirs of a Beatnik, Pieces of a Song: Selected Poems).
entities: The Fall of America: Poems of These States
A Coney Island of the Mind
